title: One call-transport contract: the shell branches on capability, never provider
deviations_from_card: (1) Case 7, the critic revision: the start() dispatch `if (c.provider === "openai")` is kept as the ONE permitted provider-keyed line, because opening a session takes engine-specific inputs (SDP exchange vs SDK signed URL). The source check expects exactly 1 [!=]== "elevenlabs|openai" match, requires it to be that dispatch, and requires no `providerRef` (removed; failover now just calls setProvider). (2) isSpeaking was dropped from the contract. Both transports already push the speaking flag through setSpeaking (the ElevenLabs onMode hook, and the OpenAI analyser), so the render reads one state flag, renamed oaiSpeaking to interviewerSpeaking. The SDK's isSpeaking is `mode === "speaking"`, which is the same signal. (3) Added stopCapture() and a stable `handle` to the contract. stopCapture is the OpenAI mic-stop in the closing-answer grace. handle replaces `isActiveProvider: providerRef === "elevenlabs"` with `transportRef.current?.handle === elSession`, where elSession = sessionFromRef(conversationRef) is held stable in useState. (4) The level-sampling rAF loop is owned by a shell effect keyed on phase live|ending plus capabilities.levels === "sampled", not by the adapter. This keeps the adapter node-testable, and the loop dies with the phase even on a drop where end() is never called. Its cleanup zeroes the box. (5) Adapter factories live in call-transport.ts. openai.ts is unchanged. elevenlabs.ts only lost the now-dead sendElevenLabsDirective, whose logic moved into the adapter. (6) VoiceInterview.tsx grew by 17 lines (1449 to 1466) instead of shrinking by 60 to 90. The inline branches became one-liners, but the sampling effect and the comments explaining the seam were added.
notes: SEAM for wave-2 slot B (edits finalize()/start()): transportRef is cleared in start()'s per-attempt reset, next to sessionIdRef/sessionTokenRef = null, and set in the dispatch just before startOpenAiCall / startElevenLabsSession. finalize() asks planEnd(transport?.capabilities, {pendingCandidate, channelOpen}) only when status === completed. end() asks planEnd and, on endSessionThenWaitMs, calls transport.end() and arms the fallback timer. Unmount and the connect timeout call transportRef.current?.end(), which is idempotent. The EL_DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS and OAI_FINAL_TURN_GRACE_MS constants moved to call-transport.ts. Behaviour change worth knowing: the SDK callbacks are now ignored while a new attempt has no transport yet. Before, a late onDisconnect from an earlier ElevenLabs attempt could finalize the new attempt during its /connect round-trip. Server contract untouched (ADR 0010, /complete, no wire change). Tests use fake transports, and @elevenlabs/react is never imported under node. tsc: 0 errors in my files; the whole-tree run is red only on foreign paths (untracked kpi-sim/, and the in-flight sibling edit app/_lib/analyze-run.test.ts). Full test:unit exit 1, only on sibling in-flight files: analyze-run, applicant-profile-timeout, python-runner-*, rediscovery-tenancy, extract-text, winnability-spawn-timeout, match/engine-busy, profile-spawn-timeout, devcases/outboxView. All 127 voice tests are green. test:perf exit 1, only on app/api/agents/hire-from-need/route.ts (+1 module / +14 KB). `--explain` shows no voice or call-transport module in that graph, so the growth is a sibling's uncommitted python-runner or rediscovery work, not mine. VoiceInterview is reached only through dynamic imports. eslint: 0 errors, plus 1 warning that was already there (lockSettings dep on the probe effect). Doc commit taken and released under the lock. loop_open: none, because the change adds no refusal, gate or stored status. The orb (InterviewPresence) is the only display the levels feed, and it now receives them on both engines. Not verified in a live browser call: no dev server or keys, per the rules.
